title: gpu-oom-debug-notes-raja-singh
content:
Context / summary:
- Intermittent CUDA OOMs observed on prod-dedicated-gpu-02 while serving long-chat sessions (context ~ 16k).
- Errors seen both in python worker logs and system dmesg (oom-killer). Suspect a mix of true OOM (memory pressure) + occasional driver/runtime mismatch causing allocation failures.

Timeline / breadcrumbs:
- 2026-02-10 09:12 UTC: First repro during load test (batch size 4, seq_len ~1500). Worker crashed with RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory.
  - Python stack snippet: RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.8 GiB (GPU 0; 47.68 GiB total capacity; 46.02 GiB already allocated; 0 bytes free)
- 2026-02-10 09:13 UTC: syslog shows: "[ 12345.678901] Out of memory: Killed process 9876 (python3) total-vm:..."
- 2026-02-11 02:04 UTC: Noticed occasional: "CUDA error: unknown error" and driver mismatch logs in container: "NVIDIA-SMI has failed because it couldn't communicate with the NVIDIA driver."
- 2026-02-12 15:32 UTC: On one node got: "cudaGetDevice() failed: CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version" after a hot-patch (kernel + nvidia-driver update)

Commands run / logs captured (quick copy):
- nvidia-smi -a:
  GPU 0: A100-SXM4-80GB
  Driver Version: 535.54.03
  CUDA Version: 12.1

- docker exec -it worker ps aux | grep python
- tail -n 200 /var/log/syslog | grep -i oom
- dmesg | grep -i nvidia
- python -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available()); print(torch.version.cuda); print(torch.cuda.memory_summary())"
  Output: True, 11.7, (memory summary showing ~46 GB allocated before failure on the process)

Observed error snippets:
- RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.2 GiB (GPU 0; 47.68 GiB total capacity; 46.02 GiB already allocated; 0 bytes free)
- RuntimeError: CUDA error: CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED when calling `cublasCreate( &handle )`
- CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version
- /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so.11.0: version `CUDART_11.0' not found (required by /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvrtc.so.11.2)

Hypotheses:
- H1: True OOM due to insufficient per-process memory for long context + naive KV cache + batch size. We should instrument per-request token allocations.
- H2: Memory leak in our kernel/extension path (custom CUDA kernel used for fused attention) leading to gradual increase in device memory across requests. Check allocations over time.
- H3: Driver / runtime mismatch on some nodes: after kernel/pinning/driver upgrades, some containers pick up incompatible libcuda/libcudart causing allocation failures reported as unknown errors.
- H4: Container uses host drivers but an older CUDA toolkit in the image causing symbol mismatches between libcudart and libnvrtc.

Mitigations / fixes tried (and results):
- Reduce batch size and context length in load test -> reduces OOM frequency but not eliminate in long-run tests. (Partial)
- Set torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = False and enable torch.cuda.empty_cache() between requests -> no measurable improvement.
- Add explicit gc.collect() and torch.cuda.synchronize() after big allocations -> mitigates immediate leak symptoms in dev but not prod.
- Restarting nvidia-persistenced and the container -> temporarily fixes "NVIDIA-SMI cannot communicate" errors on one node.
- Reinstalled nvidia driver to 535.86.05 on affected nodes -> reduced driver mismatch errors but need monitoring.
- Switched some workers to CUDA 11.7 runtime image (matching torch build) -> removed the libcudart mismatch error in those workers.

Investigation next steps / checklist:
- [ ] Add per-worker ephemeral endpoint to dump torch.cuda.memory_reserved / memory_allocated periodically and emit to metrics (prom gauge).
- [ ] Add compatibility check at container startup: compare driver version (nvidia-smi) vs torch.version.cuda and log if mismatch > 1 major version. Fail fast or route to safe pool.
- [ ] Run long-running soak test with debug build of fused kernels (with extra checks / debug alloc tracking).
- [ ] Audit container images: ensure libcudart in image is consistent with expected CUDA runtime used by torch. Pin base image to official nvidia/cuda X.Y and test.
- [ ] Reproduce with reduced repro script: small looped generation with manual flush of KV cache to see memory trend.
- [ ] Try enabling per-process memory fraction limit: torch.cuda.set_per_process_memory_fraction(0.95, device=0) as an experiment.
- [ ] Investigate NCCL errors in logs - could indicate driver-level instability under high throughput.

Quick debugging commands to run next on affected node:
- docker run --gpus all --rm -it --entrypoint /bin/bash <image>
- python -c "import torch, time
print(torch.version.cuda, torch.cuda.get_device_name(0))
for i in range(100):
  t0 = time.time()
  x = torch.randn((64,1024,1024), device='cuda', dtype=torch.float16)
  del x
  torch.cuda.empty_cache()
  print(i, torch.cuda.memory_reserved(), torch.cuda.memory_allocated(), time.time()-t0)
"
- LD_DEBUG=files python -c 'import ctypes; ctypes.CDLL("/usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so")'  # check if loader finds expected lib

Notes / random observations:
- A100 shows 80GB but usable memory is slightly less; our allocator + fragmentation leads to early OOMs if many allocations are non-contiguous. Consider max_split_size_mb and trying with split allocator environment flags.
- We have multiple CUDA/toolkit versions across images (11.7 vs 12.1). Need standardization.
- On one repro run, manually triggering torch.cuda.empty_cache() freed a few GBs but not enough. Suggest we add pre-request cache trimming for long sessions.

Decisions / temporary mitigations to deploy:
- Pin serving image to CUDA 11.7 / cuDNN variant matching torch wheel for next deploy to the problematic pool.
- Add early-start compatibility check that logs and routes failing nodes to a quarantine pool for SRE to repro.

Open questions:
- Is the fused attention kernel leaking GPU memory across forward passes? (ask @Miguel to run debug build)
- Should we reduce default max context or enforce per-tenant quotas to avoid noisy neighbors causing OOMs?

References / links (internal):
- infra: node maint runbook: confluence:infra/node-maint
- PR with fused kernel debugging: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/482

Notes to self: when I come back to this doc: try to produce a minimal repro in <1h and show memory trend line to SRE + kernel author.

--- end of notes ---
